slides.title: NextPlay Kids
slides.subtitle:
Every child deserves a place to play.
Youth sports commerce, programs & safety — ages 2 to 17.
Investor Brief · September 2026 · Mumbai
slides.notes: Open with the mission: we are building the trusted sports layer for India's 350M+ children. One line: we make sports safer, more accessible and development-focused for ages 2-17, through gear, programs and technology.

slides.title: The Problem

bullets.text: Parents cannot trust what they buy
Adult-sized gear sold to children; no honest age ranges; 60%+ of youth sports gear is sized wrongly (industry estimate)
Sports drop-off is massive — and expensive
70% of kids quit organised sport by age 13 (Aspen Institute). Pressure culture, wrong equipment, boring first experiences.
No trusted marketplace for ages 2-17
General sports retailers sell adult gear smaller; nobody owns the child-development layer: right gear, right age, right challenge.
Schools & academies run on spreadsheets
Rosters, attendance, parent messaging and equipment inventory are manual, unsafe and unprofitable.

slides.notes: Frame the wedge: parents don't have a trusted, age-appropriate sports partner. Retailers sell products; nobody sells development. The safety gap is the trust wedge — we win parents before we sell them.

slides.title: The Market

bullets.text: India youth sports economy — large, fragmented, under-served
Sports goods market: ~$4B+ and growing double-digit; youth segment under-penetrated
350M+ children aged 2-17; rising middle-class spend on child development
Government push: Khelo India, school sport mandates, NEP physical education
Revenue lines (multiple engines, one brand)
1. Gear e-commerce (AOV ₹1,800-4,500)  2. Programs & camps (₹4k-25k/term)  3. School & academy B2B bundles  4. SaaS dashboards  5. Digital products
Global reference: Decathlon youth line, Dick's Sporting Goods youth — none own the full child-development stack in India

slides.notes: Anchor: this is not a toy shop, it's the development layer. Multiple revenue engines de-risk: retail margins day one, programs build LTV, B2B builds stickiness, SaaS builds moat.

slides.title: The Product — Trust by Design

bullets.text: Safety-first commerce
Every product: honest age range, safety certification badge, size-true charts, fit guides co-written with paediatric physiotherapists, free size exchanges
Sports Explorer — the recommendation engine
Interactive quiz (age, interests, time, budget, accessibility) → matched sport + starter bundle. Acquisition engine disguised as a service.
Parent Dashboard & Coach Dashboard
Child profiles, progress tracking with parental-consent controls, coach messaging, attendance & inventory — parents are account holders, always.
Live prototype already shipped
16-page experience live at maheshkoriacourse.github.io/nextplay-kids — 45-product catalogue, filters, cart, dashboards. Working proof, not slides.

slides.notes: Demo the live site here if internet allows. Emphasize: parents-as-account-holders is a moat — trust compounds, and no competitor treats child data with this discipline.

slides.title: Why We Win

bullets.text: 1. Trust layer — safety certification on 100% of catalogue, fit-first commerce
Parents switch brands over safety mistakes; they never leave a brand that prevented them
2. Age-graded everything — 2-4, 5-7, 8-11, 12-14, 15-17 product & program ladders
A child who enters at 4 grows with us for 15 years — highest LTV story in Indian retail
3. Inclusive by architecture — adaptive sport woven through every category
Untapped segment; schools and parents actively searching for it
4. Founder-market fit
19+ years BFSI operations & data leadership + AI architecture. Distribution discipline of a banker, product speed of a builder.

slides.notes: The LTV ladder is the killer argument: a child at age 4 can be a customer through age 17 — 13 years of gear, programs, camps. No other Indian sports brand owns childhood this completely.

slides.title: Business Model

bullets.text: Revenue streams
Retail margin 30-45% on gear · Program fees ₹4k-25k per term · B2B school bundles (₹50k-5L contracts) · SaaS ₹500-2k/seat/month · Birthday & event services
Unit economics (target at scale)
Blended gross margin ~38% · CAC via parents-community + schools (low paid-media dependence) · Repeat: gear re-orders as children grow + term renewals
LTV engine
A child acquired at 7 through a ₹2,500 starter kit can generate ₹1.5L-3L lifetime value over a decade (gear + programs).

slides.notes: Keep it honest: these are targets, not audited numbers. The structural point is the ladder — gear is the acquisition product, programs are the retention engine, SaaS is the margin engine.

slides.title: 5-Year Path to Scale
slides.notes: Yr1: Mumbai-first, prove repeat purchase + term renewals. Yr2-3: 5 cities + 100 schools. Yr4-5: national franchise-style expansion + SaaS across academies. Numbers are a working plan, not a promise — say that out loud to investors.

slides.title: Go-To-Market

bullets.text: Phase 1 (0-12 months) — Mumbai beachhead
Shopify-style D2C launch + 3 academy partnerships + 2 school contracts. Target: 5,000 orders, ₹1.2 Cr GMV.
Growth loops, not paid-media dependence
Sports Explorer quiz (SEO magnet) → starter bundles → programs → word-of-mouth parent communities → school referrals back to retail.
Content flywheel
AI-video channel: safety guides, skill drills, child-athlete stories — built on our in-house AI film pipeline (canon-controlled production, near-zero content cost).
B2B wedge
Schools buy bundles for compliance + safety documentation; we upskill their coaches and own the relationship.

slides.notes: The AI-video content engine is the founder's unfair advantage — this team can produce studio-grade content at software cost. Mention the filmcraft studio capability.

slides.title: Technology & Data Moat

bullets.text: Age-graded recommendation engine — every sale teaches the system
Fit data (height, sport, size outcomes) compounds into India's best youth sizing dataset
Progress tracking with parental consent = retention machine
Families stay for the growth record, not just the gear
Coach SaaS creates network lock-in
Academies run attendance, rosters, inventory on our stack — switching is costly
AI content pipeline in-house
Studio-grade video production capability — marketing cost advantage competitors can't match

slides.notes: Investors hear 'data moat' too often — make it concrete: every exchanged jersey tells us a child grew 4cm. In 3 years we know fit better than any competitor in the country.

slides.title: The Ask

bullets.text: Raising: ₹3.5 Cr seed round (18-month runway)
40% Inventory & retail infrastructure · 25% Technology (dashboards, quiz engine, apps) · 20% Programs & coaching network · 15% Brand & growth
18-month milestones
₹1.2 Cr GMV · 5,000 families · 3 academies + 2 schools signed · repeat-purchase rate 35%+ · SaaS pilot with 10 academies
Round structure
SAFE / CCPS · founder-led with governance-ready reporting from day one
What you get
Early entry into the trust-layer of a ₹40,000 Cr+ market, with a founder who has managed 9-figure P&Ls and ships working product in weeks, not quarters.

slides.notes: Be direct on the number and the milestones. Invite diligence: prototype is live, security-audited stack, weekly backup discipline. Close with the mission line.
